message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <ZONE> with your preferred zone)
ZONE=us-central1-a

# 2. Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom init script
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --reservation-affinity=any \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Sets the size & performance tier of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Allows the instance to use any available GPU reservation. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules if you plan to expose services. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, just change the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` values accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to the Compute Engine Instances endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` with your actual GCP project ID. The `instance.json` file contains the JSON payload above.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project & Billing** – Ensure billing is enabled for the project.
- [ ] **API Enabled** – Enable the *Compute Engine API* in the Cloud Console or via `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`.
- [ ] **GPU Quota** – Verify you have enough GPU quota in the selected zone (`us-central1-a` in the examples). Request additional quota if necessary.
- [ ] **Firewall Rules** – The tags `http-server` and `https-server` automatically open ports 80/443. Add custom rules if you need other ports.

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and install the NVIDIA drivers:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

After reboot, verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a fully‑functional Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
